initiatives.title: Iceberg Community Syncs and Governance
initiatives.summary: A series of regular community synchronization meetings and governance votes for the Apache Iceberg project covering Spark integration, catalog features, read restrictions, index support, and metadata enhancements. The initiative includes discussions on version support deprecation, new feature specifications (variant types, Puffin format), and infrastructure improvements for the project.
key_points: Regular community syncs across multiple Iceberg workstreams including Spark integration, catalog, read restrictions, and index support
Active governance through voting on major decisions including Spark version support, metadata format changes, and new feature adoption
Ongoing technical discussions on advanced features like variant type support, Puffin format for statistics, and table-level statistics implementation

initiatives.title: Relative Paths in Iceberg Table Spec
initiatives.summary: This initiative adds support for relative paths to the Iceberg v4 specification, enabling more flexible table location handling. The proposal addresses path resolution mechanics and how table location mutability impacts lifecycle operations, with a focus on simplifying the implementation approach.
key_points: Adds relative path support to Iceberg v4 specification
Addresses table location mutability and its effects on path resolution
Simplifies implementation approach for relative path handling

initiatives.title: HostnameVerificationPolicy default in TLSConfigurer
initiatives.summary: Discussion on whether to expose HostnameVerificationPolicy in TLSConfigurer and set the default to CLIENT (current behavior, less safe) or BOTH (safer, behavioral change). Community consensus favors BOTH as the default for the 1.11 release to improve security in production environments.
key_points: Regression reported in HTTPClient TLS handling
Need to expose HostnameVerificationPolicy in TLSConfigurer
Default should be BOTH for stronger hostname verification
Community consensus reached to change default to BOTH for 1.11 release

initiatives.title: REST Spec: Clarify identifier uniqueness across catalog object types
initiatives.summary: Discussion on clarifying the REST Catalog specification regarding identifier uniqueness within namespaces. The proposal aims to make explicit that identifiers must be unique across tables and views in the same namespace, with consistent 409 Conflict error descriptions across all write operations. Community consensus emerged to enforce uniqueness only between tables and views, while keeping functions in a separate dimension to allow context-based resolution.
key_points: Current REST spec has inconsistent 409 Conflict descriptions for identifier uniqueness
Proposal to enforce cross-type uniqueness between tables and views only, not functions
Functions and indexes should be allowed to share names with tables/views based on context
Community agreed on consistent error message: 'already exists as a table or view'
Clarification is spec-only with no behavior changes for compliant catalogs

initiatives.title: Dashboard for Iceberg Design Docs and Discussions
initiatives.summary: A community member has created a static website to consolidate Iceberg design documents and related discussions from various sources into one accessible view. The initiative aims to improve navigation and understanding of ongoing project activities, and feedback is encouraged for further development.
key_points: Website consolidates design docs and discussions
Feedback and contributions are welcome

initiatives.title: REST Specification Enhancement Initiative
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive effort to expand and refine the Iceberg REST API specification through multiple feature additions including remote signing endpoints, row lineage support, encryption key updates, schema management, and various metadata fields. The initiative encompasses numerous proposals at different stages, with several features already released and many others in active voting or discussion phases.
key_points: Remote signing endpoint promotion to main REST spec with community support and active voting
Row lineage implementation requiring first-row-id field and added-rows snapshot metadata
Encryption and security enhancements including key updates and metadata integrity protection
Schema and table management improvements including RemoveSchemas, RemovePartitionSpecs, and overwriteRequested field additions
Multiple features already released including encryption key updates, row lineage requirements, and statistics property name fixes

initiatives.title: Iceberg Performance and Metadata Optimization
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative to improve Apache Iceberg's performance, scalability, and metadata efficiency through multiple complementary enhancements. This includes optimizing transaction commit rates, reducing metadata bloat, enabling parallel task execution, improving query planning with statistics, and streamlining credential management across REST and Spark interfaces.
key_points: Parallel task execution in Spark readers for improved performance with small files (76.4% improvement on S3)
Metadata optimization through delta-encoded schemas, compact JSON formatting, and manifest-level statistics to reduce storage bloat
Transaction and credential management improvements including batch endpoints, vended credential refresh, and multi-statement transaction support
REST API enhancements for partial metadata loading, bulk object lookup, and standardized credential handling
Column-level updates and efficient deletion vector handling to support ML/AI workloads and merge-on-read performance
Core API improvements including tags field for custom metadata, ROUND_ROBIN distribution mode, and explicit features declaration

initiatives.title: Iceberg Metadata and API Evolution
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative to modernize Iceberg's metadata handling, REST catalog capabilities, and API design through strategic deprecations, fine-grained metadata commits, and standardized interfaces. The effort includes removing legacy features, establishing semantic versioning policies, and enhancing the REST protocol to better support distributed metadata operations.
key_points: Deprecating legacy features (Position Deletes with Row Data, FileAppenderFactory, Spark 3.2/3.4, Spark 2.4) to streamline the codebase and reduce maintenance burden
Implementing fine-grained metadata commits in REST catalog to shift snapshot production from clients to server, improving consistency and enabling better transaction semantics
Enhancing metadata infrastructure with table labels, decoupled timestamps, and improved snapshot reference handling to support operational context and prevent race conditions
Standardizing APIs across implementations (FileFormat API, FileIO interfaces) and establishing semantic versioning guarantees for post-1.0 stability

initiatives.title: Apache Iceberg Release Planning
initiatives.summary: A series of release discussions and planning for multiple versions of Apache Iceberg across 1.4.2 through 1.10.2, including patch releases for correctness issues and regressions, with PyIceberg 0.6.0 successfully released. These discussions track important features, fixes, and changes intended for inclusion in each respective release.
key_points: Multiple concurrent release tracks from 1.4.2 to 1.10.2
Focus on correctness issues and regression fixes in patch releases
PyIceberg 0.6.0 successfully released
Ongoing discussion and planning for future versions

initiatives.title: Apache Iceberg Release Coordination
initiatives.summary: Coordinating multiple patch and minor releases across Apache Iceberg and its language implementations (Java, Python, Rust, Go) to address bug fixes, security vulnerabilities, and feature completeness. Release managers are tracking milestones, backporting fixes, and managing release candidates across various version branches.
key_points: Multiple active releases in progress: Iceberg 1.11.0 (Java), PyIceberg 0.11.0, iceberg-rust 0.9, and various patch releases (1.10.2, 1.10.1, 1.9.2, 1.8.1, 1.7.2, 1.6.2)
Security focus includes CVE fixes (CVE-2025-30065, CVE-2024-47561) and CVE scanning implementation in CI/release pipelines
Cross-implementation standardization efforts for error handling, error messages, and REST API specifications across Java, Python, Rust, and Go clients

initiatives.title: Fine-Grained Access Control Implementation
initiatives.summary: This initiative encompasses the design and implementation of fine-grained access control (FGAC) for Iceberg, including row-level and column-level restrictions, data masking, and secure view support through REST catalog specifications. The community has progressed from initial proposals through specification design and is working on standardizing data masks, execution order for read restrictions, and integration with query engines.
key_points: Implementing row and column-level access control with data masking in Iceberg REST catalogs
Standardizing read restrictions execution order: authorization predicates, row filters, column masks, then user query filters
Designing pre-defined data masks and deciding between Action model versus full Transform approach
Adding support for secure DEFINER views through loaded-via field in loadTable requests
Ensuring interoperability between Iceberg REST catalogs and various query engines

key_points: Regular community sync meetings held to discuss project updates and technical developments
Multiple regional community meetups organized across Europe, North America, and Asia
Structured discussions for new contributors and project-specific working groups like Rust and PyIceberg
Community governance discussions on documentation, API stability, and specification clarifications

initiatives.title: Iceberg V3 Specification and Delete Operations
initiatives.summary: This initiative encompasses multiple proposals to enhance Iceberg's V3 specification and delete operation handling, including improvements to deletion vectors, position deletes, row lineage, and related metadata. Key efforts focus on deprecating equality deletes in favor of position deletes and deletion vectors, standardizing metrics and metadata fields, and improving REST API capabilities for scan planning and credential management.
key_points: Transition from equality deletes to deletion vectors and position deletes as primary delete mechanisms in V3
Enhancements to REST API scan planning including storage credentials, row counts, and improved metadata reporting
Standardization of snapshot metadata, metrics, and optional fields across implementations
Row lineage support as a required feature in V3, with mutual exclusivity from equality deletes
Improvements to delete file handling, including RowId-based deletion and conversion mechanisms for CDC support

initiatives.title: Iceberg Documentation and Project Infrastructure
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative to improve Iceberg's documentation, specification clarity, and project infrastructure. This includes restructuring documentation organization, standardizing terminology and style guides, enhancing authentication documentation, and establishing better processes for specification changes and releases.
key_points: Clarify specification terminology (column-id, field-id, source-id) and document the Table Specification lifecycle process
Consolidate and restructure documentation including navigation, style standardization (Microsoft Style Guide), and moving docs into main repository
Enhance authentication documentation with OAuth2 guides and formalize 'Trusted Iceberg Client' terminology for REST Catalog
Improve project communication through blogs, release notes, and implementation status pages across multiple language libraries
Establish better development processes including markdown linting, documentation requirements, and clearer release communication

initiatives.title: Replace MinIO with Alternative S3 Backend
initiatives.summary: Initiative to replace MinIO with a more actively maintained S3-compatible storage solution in both test infrastructure and quick start demos. The proposals evaluate alternatives like SeaweedFS and RustFS to improve test reliability and address MinIO's maintenance mode status.
key_points: MinIO is in maintenance mode and needs replacement
Evaluating S3-compatible alternatives (SeaweedFS, RustFS) for test backend and demos
Aims to improve test reliability for credential and IAM/STS flow scenarios

Regular patch and minor releases with bug fixes and improvements

Maintenance of multiple stable versions with backported fixes

initiatives.title: Iceberg Project Modernization and Maintenance
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative to modernize the Iceberg codebase by upgrading Java and Rust versions, improving testing infrastructure, managing dependencies across multiple runtime versions, and enhancing developer tooling. The effort spans multiple language ecosystems (Java, Python, Rust) and focuses on reducing technical debt while maintaining compatibility across supported versions.
key_points: Java modernization: Migrating to Java 17+ features, dropping Java 8/11 support, and adopting modern syntax patterns like switch expressions and instanceof patterns
Multi-version compatibility management: Maintaining feature parity across Spark 3.4/3.5/4.0, Flink versions, and Hive versions while deprecating older unsupported versions
Testing and build infrastructure improvements: Implementing parallel test execution, REST Catalog compatibility testing automation, and ASF Develocity integration for build scan analysis
Dependency and ecosystem modernization: Addressing PyIceberg optional dependencies, Rust MSRV policy, logging framework upgrades, and JUnit5 migration
Release planning: Coordinating multiple releases including Iceberg 1.10.0, iceberg-rust 0.5.0, and managing deprecation timelines for older components

initiatives.title: Support sort order in CTAS/RTAS via TBLPROPERTIES
initiatives.summary: Feature request to allow specifying sort order during CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) and REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT (RTAS) operations in Spark SQL, avoiding the need for separate ALTER TABLE commands. Current workarounds either create temporary empty table windows or require double writes, both causing operational issues. Proposes using TBLPROPERTIES as the channel to pass sort order information since Spark's DSv2 StagingTableCatalog lacks a native sort order parameter.
key_points: Current sort order setup requires separate ALTER TABLE command after table creation
Option A (empty table window) makes table temporarily unavailable to consumers
Option B (double write) doubles compute cost and storage churn
Proposes using TBLPROPERTIES to pass sort order during CTAS/RTAS
Requires changes in Spark Catalog with parseSortOrder pattern from rewrite_data_files

initiatives.title: Iceberg Specification and Feature Enhancements
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative encompassing multiple proposals to enhance Apache Iceberg's specification and core functionality, including materialized views, secondary indexes, metadata management, REST API improvements, and schema-aware operations. The proposals address query optimization, data migration, catalog federation, and specification clarifications across v3/v4 versions and various language implementations.
key_points: Materialized views implementation with lineage tracking, refresh state management, and external table handling
Secondary indexes using Bloom filters in Puffin format for file-skipping and query optimization
REST API enhancements including events endpoint for catalog federation, metadata statistics management, and scan planning modes
Metadata and schema improvements: linking schema IDs to data files, optional metadata.json writing, table name persistence, and column metrics tracking
Specification refinements for v3/v4 including snapshot lifecycle management, partition spec handling, and identity partition column reading/writing requirements

initiatives.title: Iceberg V3 Specification Enhancements
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative to refine and complete the Iceberg V3 specification, including support for new data types (Variant, Geometry), type promotion mechanisms, metadata encoding improvements, and clarifications on file system table handling. Most proposals have been voted on and released, with a few remaining implementation gaps in the Java API.
key_points: Variant type support with field bounds and array metadata differentiation
Geometry and Geography type enhancements including wraparound restriction clarification
Type promotion from date to timestamp and unknown type handling in V3
Simplified multi-argument field-id encoding for improved efficiency
File system table specification clarification and Java API implementation gaps

initiatives.title: REST Catalog quota exceeded on public dataset
initiatives.summary: User encountered a 429 rate limit error when loading a table from the Iceberg public dataset, hitting the IRCReadRequestsPerMinutePerProject quota of 300 requests per minute. The discussion addresses quota limitations and potential solutions for accessing the public dataset through BigLake's REST Catalog.
key_points: REST Catalog read requests quota limit of 300 per minute is easily exceeded
Error occurs when loading tables from public dataset
BigLake offers free tier with 50,000 free requests per month
Users can request higher quota limits through Google Cloud documentation

initiatives.title: Apache Iceberg Community Governance
initiatives.summary: This initiative encompasses community management activities including committer and PMC member promotions, establishment of community guidelines and processes, and coordination of release voting procedures. It reflects the project's maturation in formalizing governance structures and community participation standards.
key_points: Multiple committer and PMC member promotions recognizing contributor achievements
Establishment of community guidelines based on Apache Way principles
Formalization of processes for community decisions like Slack plugin management and release voting

initiatives.title: Iceberg SQL Extensions and Expression System
initiatives.summary: This initiative aims to extend Iceberg's SQL capabilities and expression system to support Iceberg-specific operations, maintenance tasks, and advanced predicates. It encompasses standardizing SQL syntax across query engines, enhancing expression structures with function calls and new predicates, and exposing functionality like data compaction through unified SQL interfaces.
key_points: Extend Iceberg expressions to support function calls, UDFs, and new predicates like StringContains and StringEndsWith
Standardize SQL syntax extensions across query engines for table maintenance and Iceberg-specific operations
Introduce data compaction strategies and other Iceberg-specific functionality through SQL extensions
Consider cross-engine interoperability approaches including UUID type support and potential Substrait adoption for views

initiatives.title: Spark Function for Column Undeletion
initiatives.summary: Frank proposes adding a Spark function to undelete columns in Iceberg, with a PR that allows undeletion of non-nullable columns by making them optional upon rollback. This extends beyond the spec's strict requirements but represents a reasonable tradeoff for usability.
key_points: Adds Spark function for column undeletion capability
Allows undeletion of non-nullable columns by making them optional
Extends spec requirements which only allow undeletion for nullable fields or unchanged snapshots
Seeking community feedback on the proposed approach

initiatives.title: Standardizing Glue StorageDescriptor column opt-out
initiatives.summary: Proposal to add a `glue.schema-columns` property across Iceberg implementations to allow omitting columns from StorageDescriptor, addressing AWS Glue API payload size limits for large schemas (~3600 fields). The author seeks consensus on naming convention and whether this should be a coordinated cross-implementation effort or per-implementation under the `glue.*` namespace.
key_points: Large schema tables fail CreateTable/UpdateTable due to Glue API payload size limits when all columns are written to StorageDescriptor
Previous attempts in Java (#11334, #12664) were closed without consensus
Proposes `glue.schema-columns` property (default: true) with fail-fast guard when Lake Formation is enabled
Go implementation already available with Lake Formation guard
Seeking alignment on naming and coordination strategy across Java, Python, Go, and Rust implementations

initiatives.title: Apache Iceberg Language Bindings Releases
initiatives.summary: This initiative encompasses the release cycles for Apache Iceberg's Go and C++ language bindings across multiple versions. Multiple release candidates have been voted on, with several successfully passing community votes while others were vetoed and abandoned during the release process.
key_points: Go bindings released through v0.5.0 with successful community votes
C++ bindings progressing with v0.2.0 RC2 released and v0.1.0 RC4 in voting
Multiple release candidates vetoed and abandoned, indicating iterative refinement of release quality
Active community participation with binding and non-binding votes on release candidates

initiatives.title: Docker Images and Testing Infrastructure
initiatives.summary: The Iceberg community is working to standardize and centralize Docker image publishing and testing infrastructure across multiple projects and integrations. This includes establishing maintained Docker images for REST catalog adapters, Spark/Flink integrations, and quick-start environments, along with implementing consistent testing frameworks and repository management practices.
key_points: Centralizing Docker image publishing from Iceberg GitHub repo for Spark, Flink, and REST catalog testing
Standardizing cross-client integration tests through unified Docker image framework
Establishing community-maintained Docker images for quick-start environments and adapters
Evaluating hosting options (GitHub Packages vs DockerHub) for Apache Iceberg images
Implementing repository management improvements including merge queues and stale issue automation

initiatives.title: Iceberg Maintenance and Replication Capabilities
initiatives.summary: This initiative expands Iceberg's operational capabilities by adding local maintenance actions, URL rewriting for disaster recovery, incremental replication across datacenters, Flink-based maintenance task execution, and streaming reads for V2 tables. Together, these features enable more flexible deployment models, improved data reliability, and real-time data warehouse use cases.
key_points: Add non-distributed thread-pool-backed actions for lightweight CLI and local maintenance tasks
Implement URL prefix rewriting for dynamic path transformation during data access and disaster recovery testing
Enable incremental replication with optional commit workflow integration for cross-datacenter backup and data locality
Support Flink execution of maintenance operations (file rewriting, manifest management, snapshot expiration) in streaming and batch contexts
Enable incremental streaming reads of Iceberg V2 tables for quasi-real-time data warehouse scenarios

initiatives.title: PyIceberg 0.11.1 patch release for REST Catalog regression
initiatives.summary: A proposal to cut a 0.11.1 patch release to fix a critical regression in PyIceberg 0.11.0 where stricter ConfigResponse validation crashes when connecting to Apache Polaris 1.2.0+ due to missing HTTP methods like PUT in the HttpMethod enum. The fix has already been merged to main and is needed urgently since users upgrading to 0.11.0 with Polaris hit a hard crash on startup with no workaround.
key_points: 0.11.0 introduced stricter validation that breaks RestCatalog initialization with Apache Polaris
HttpMethod enum was missing PUT and other standard HTTP methods
Polaris extends the REST Catalog spec with additional PUT endpoints
Fix already merged in PR #3010 to main branch
Critical regression affecting widely-used Polaris catalog implementation

initiatives.title: Remove HDFS trash behavior from FileIO
initiatives.summary: Discussion on whether to remove HDFS trash behavior from Iceberg's HadoopFileIO. The proposer argues that trash functionality is confusing, doesn't fit the FileIO interface, poses data governance risks, and is unnecessary since Iceberg already maintains table history for recovery.
key_points: Trash behavior is a client responsibility in Hadoop, not part of FileSystem interface, making it inappropriate for FileIO
Trash could leak sensitive data by moving deleted files to user home directories, conflicting with governance requirements
Iceberg's built-in table history provides better recovery mechanism than trash folders for accidental deletes
Trash behavior is confusing and not obvious to FileIO users

initiatives.title: Expose abortTransaction method on public API
initiatives.summary: Discussion about whether to expose transaction abort functionality on the public Transaction API. The Hive project needs to clean up partial changes when multi-table transactions fail to acquire locks, currently handled by BaseTransaction.cleanUpOnCommitFailure. Proposal is to add a public abortTransaction() method rather than just making the existing cleanup method protected.
key_points: Hive team needs to revert partial changes when multi-table transactions fail
Current cleanup handled by BaseTransaction.cleanUpOnCommitFailure
Two options: make method protected or expose new public abortTransaction() method
Public API approach is more explicit and natural

initiatives.title: REST spec mismatch for Boolean Expressions
initiatives.summary: A mismatch was discovered between the REST API specification and the ExpressionParser implementation for boolean expressions. The spec defines them as wrapped objects like {"type": "true"}, but the parser expects plain booleans, causing filter parsing failures. A PR has been opened to align the REST spec with the actual parser implementation.
key_points: REST scan planning APIs fail when parsing filters with boolean expressions
Spec defines boolean expressions as wrapped objects but parser expects plain booleans
PR proposes updating REST spec to match ExpressionParser behavior
Alternative approach of changing Java representation was considered

Metadata management improvements including etag support for CommitTableResponse and commit timestamps in CommitReport

Freshness-aware table loading with min-rows-requested and planId query parameters for optimized data access
Namespace separator configurability and view registration support across catalogs

initiatives.title: Missing-column handling in StrictMetricsEvaluator with schema evolution
initiatives.summary: Discussion on handling missing columns in StrictMetricsEvaluator after schema evolution by introducing a maxFieldId on DataFile. The proposal uses the file's maxFieldId to determine if a column existed when the file was written, enabling more accurate metrics evaluation for evolved schemas.

Columns with field id greater than maxFieldId are treated as non-existent in the file
isNull and isNotNaN return ROWS_MUST_MATCH for missing columns; other operations conservatively return ROWS_MIGHT_NOT_MATCH

initiatives.title: Adding Partition Stats Updates to REST TableUpdate Spec
initiatives.summary: Discussion about merging a correction to the REST specification to include partition stats update types in TableUpdate. The spec already defined these types but forgot to reference them in TableUpdate, causing issues for generated clients. This is treated as a spec correction oversight rather than a new feature.
key_points: Partition stats commit update types were defined but missing from TableUpdate references
Causes problems for generated clients
Treated as spec correction, not requiring a vote
PR #15115 pending merge after community feedback period

initiatives.title: Standardize UUID types in REST Catalog specification
initiatives.summary: Proposal to change UUID fields in the REST Catalog Spec from inconsistent string and UUIDTypeValue representations to a unified UUID type. This improves OpenAPI tooling support for documentation and client generation while reflecting server-side behavior that already treats these fields as UUIDs.
key_points: Current spec treats UUIDs inconsistently as strings or complex UUIDTypeValue objects
Standardizing to UUID type improves OpenAPI ecosystem tool support
Not a breaking change since servers already validate UUIDs
Makes specification accurately reflect actual server-side behavior

initiatives.title: Add assert-last-sequence-number requirement to REST API
initiatives.summary: Proposal to add a new assert-last-sequence-number update requirement to the Iceberg REST API spec to handle concurrent commits. This requirement would validate the table's sequence number hasn't advanced past the snapshot being committed, converting non-retryable ValidationException errors into retryable CommitFailedException errors in concurrent scenarios.
key_points: Concurrent commits through REST catalog cause sequence number conflicts resulting in non-retryable ValidationException
New assert-last-sequence-number requirement would validate sequence number state before commit
Converts concurrent conflicts into retryable CommitFailedException for automatic retry capability
Requirement includes type enum and last-sequence-number integer property

initiatives.title: Iceberg Repository and Module Naming

initiatives.title: Preserve commit history when adding new engine versions
initiatives.summary: Discussion on how to maintain git commit history when adding support for new engine versions. Currently, copying files from old versions to new directories loses historical context. The proposer suggests renaming the old version to the new one first, then creating a copy as the old version to preserve traceability.
key_points: Copying files loses git commit history and makes it hard to track changes
Current approach requires searching old paths which may have been deleted
Proposed solution: rename old version to new version, then copy as old version
Example given: for Spark 3.3, rename 3.2 to 3.3, copy 3.3 to 3.2, then modify

initiatives.title: Estimating byte size for unclosed ORC writers
initiatives.summary: Discussion on the correct approach to estimate byte size from unclosed ORC file writers in Iceberg's write path. The proposal involves a three-step estimation method: summing stripe offset and length, using TreeWriter's estimateMemory for buffered data, and accounting for unbuffered rows. The author questions whether using batch size directly is accurate for variable-width data types and raises concerns about TreeWriter API exposure.
key_points: ORC writers cannot roll over to new files when reaching byte size threshold due to inability to estimate unclosed writer size
Three-step estimation approach: persisted stripe bytes, memory-encoded batch data, and unbuffered batch data
Concern that batch.size estimation may be inaccurate for variable-width data types like String and Timestamp
TreeWriter and estimateMemory method are not publicly exposed in ORC Writer API

initiatives.title: Evaluate Immutables library adoption for Iceberg
initiatives.summary: Proposal to introduce the Immutables library (Apache License 2.0) to Iceberg via annotation processing for generating immutable, type-safe, and thread-safe value classes. The library would reduce boilerplate code, provide automatic builder generation, and enable JSON serialization/deserialization support, particularly beneficial for the REST-based Catalog implementation.
key_points: Immutables library generates immutable implementation classes from annotated abstract value classes
Reduces boilerplate code for getters, setters, hashCode, equals, and toString methods
Provides automatic builder classes and JSON serialization/deserialization support
Ensures thread-safety and null-safety with mandatory attribute validation
Proof-of-concept implementations shown in TableIdentifier/Namespace and TableMetadata PRs

initiatives.title: Reference names in TableIdentifier for snapshot tagging
initiatives.summary: Discussion on how to handle reference names (branches/tags) in TableIdentifier to distinguish between tables on different branches, such as namespace.tbl (default branch) versus namespace.tbl@dev (specific branch). The proposal also addresses cache invalidation challenges when multiple branch references exist for the same table.
key_points: Need to distinguish table references by branch/tag in TableIdentifier syntax
Cache invalidation complexity with multiple branch references for same table
Design considerations documented in shared Google Doc

initiatives.title: Improve Spark configuration handling and consistency
initiatives.summary: Discussion on refactoring Spark configuration management to address scattered configs across multiple classes, code duplication in parsing logic, and inconsistent precedence order between read/write options, session configs, and table metadata. Proposes consolidating configs into dedicated classes and standardizing precedence to read option → session conf → table metadata, which may be a breaking change.
key_points: SQL configs scattered across SparkUtil, IcebergSource, SparkWriteBuilder, Spark3Util should be consolidated into dedicated classes like SparkReadOptions and SparkWriteOptions
Significant code duplication in parsing read/write options, session configs, and table metadata across multiple classes and Spark 2/3 integrations
Config resolution logic complicates writer and scan builders; should be extracted to separate classes
Inconsistent precedence order for configs; proposal to standardize to read option → session conf → table metadata, which is a potential behavior change

initiatives.title: Forward compatibility and snapshot ID inheritance strategy
initiatives.summary: Discussion on how to handle snapshot ID inheritance as an optional field without breaking forward compatibility with older readers. Proposes using feature flags to allow early adoption of breaking changes within a format version, rather than immediately bumping the format version.
key_points: Snapshot ID inheritance makes the snapshot ID field optional in manifests, which breaks forward compatibility with older readers
Format version bump would break compatibility for all tables, even those not using appended manifests
Proposed solution: use feature flags to opt tables into breaking changes, allowing gradual adoption and format v2 to standardize the feature
This strategy enables releasing format features early behind flags before they become mandatory in a new format version
